key_insight: A large-scale toxicity map showed that both clinical context and inherited genetics can help predict which cancer patients are most likely to experience serious treatment-related side effects.
clinical_relevance: This work supports pre-treatment risk assessment to help clinicians personalize therapy choices and monitor higher-risk patients more closely.
method: Built MSK-Tox from >50,000 patients using an LLM-based pipeline to extract toxicity incidence, timing, and grade.
Analyzed six key adverse events across cancers and treatment regimens.
Linked clinical predictors and germline variants to toxicity risk, including therapy-specific and cross-therapy patterns.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports population-scale analysis across more than 50,000 patients, with evaluation of six representative toxicities and genetic associations such as FOXE1 and HLA-DRB1*15.
watch_item: Findings are based on retrospective data extraction and association analyses, so prospective validation is needed before routine clinical implementation.
paper_title: Population-Scale Precision Safety in Oncology Reveals Clinical and Genetic Determinants of Systemic Therapy Toxicity
